idiom_name: registry dict of implementations + factory function (Protocol/ABC DAO interfaces)
implementation_notes: The DAO interface is a Protocol or abc.ABC and the factory is a dict mapping store keys to implementation classes or partial-bound constructors, plus one small function that raises a clear error for unknown keys; duck typing means callers only need the method names to line up, so no class hierarchy is warranted. The store-selection half is often already provided - SQLAlchemy's create_engine("postgresql+psycopg://...") picks the dialect from the URL scheme and DB-API drivers share a connection shape - so DAOs take the engine or connection and stay store-agnostic. Escalate to a factory class only when implementations need construction arguments a shared factory signature cannot express.
pitfalls: Protocols are structural and checked only by type checkers; a misspelled DAO method is not caught at import time, so contract tests over every registered implementation are the real guard.
Registry lambdas capturing configuration at import time freeze early state; build implementations at the composition root or with functools.partial instead of in module scope.

sqlite3 connections are thread-bound and DB-API connections are generally not thread-safe; a family handing one connection to several threads corrupts state - pair the factory with a per-thread or per-request handle.

variants.name: Entry-point plugin discovery
variants.implementation_notes: For pluggable stores, DAO implementations advertise themselves as entry points in their packaging metadata (group myapp.daos, name equal to the store key) and the application resolves the group at startup with importlib.metadata.entry_points(group=...), loading only the configured provider - the same mechanism SQLAlchemy uses for its dialect registry. This replaces the hand-maintained dict for third-party extensions while staying a dict lookup internally; keep built-in implementations in the group too so one code path serves every store.
pitfalls: entry_points() returns different shapes across versions (selectable in 3.12+, dict-like earlier); pass group= explicitly and pin the supported API.
Loading a plugin imports third-party code at startup, so a broken plugin breaks the application - wrap .load() in a clear error boundary.
Entry-point names are global to the environment; two installed distributions registering the same store name collide silently.
